text:
Kai Li: Quick follow-up from the materialization RFC — we need to pick a path for dashboard tiles + RBAC checks. two axes: materialize cadence (5m / 30m / hourly) and auth check point (materialize-time vs request-time).
Maria Gomez: +1 to decide sooner. ops wants predictable cost, product wants low-latency loads.
Samir Patel: If we do request-time auth checks we keep tiles sharable across tenants (less storage) but higher per-request CPU for auth.
Dinesh Rao: ops POV: request-time checks increase tail latency and complicate caching layers. materialize-time auth means more writes/invalidation on role changes.
Kai Li: Agreed. Also security note — materialize-time checks risk stale perms -> potential over-exposure if we reuse tiles across tenants.
Maria Gomez: Proposal: hybrid default: materialize scoped tiles for high-sensitivity queries (tenant-scoped) and shared tiles for low-sensitivity aggregated data, with request-time final gate for edge cases.
Samir Patel: Sounds reasonable. How do we classify sensitivity? heuristics based on query shape + fields; product can opt-in explicit flag in dashboard config.
Kai Li: Minimal API change: dashboard config adds: "materialization: { cadence: \"5m\", scope: \"auto|tenant|shared\" }". Example: 
```
materialization:
  cadence: 5m
  scope: auto  # auto => use heuristics
  auth_check: runtime  # runtime|materialize|hybrid
```
Dinesh Rao: For rollout, we should default to: cadence=30m, scope=auto, auth_check=runtime. That minimizes blast radius.
Maria Gomez: Ok — product can opt dashboards into faster cadence / materialize-scoped if they need latency. We'll surface cost warning in Console.
Samir Patel: Perf test plan: run a mixed workload with request-time auth vs materialize auth for 100k tile reads/min and measure p95. I can own the loadtest.
Kai Li: Action items: 1) Samir to run perf tests (start this week) 2) Dinesh to validate invalidation path and role-change propagation (pre-prod) 3) Maria to add opt-in flags + console warning 4) Kai to sketch RBAC metadata model for tiles.
Samir Patel: I'll kick off a /run loadtest job and post results.
Dinesh Rao: Noting risk: role-change storm could create invalidation floods; recommend rate-limit invalidations and fallback to runtime auth when invalidation backlog > threshold.
Kai Li: Good call — add fallback policy to spec. I'll draft RFC follow-up with the hybrid design and fallback heuristics.
Maria Gomez: :thumbsup: Please include cost/latency numbers when available.
deploy-bot: Scheduled job created: perf/loadtest-dashboard-authz-1767 (ETA 48h).
Kai Li: Thanks — will reconvene once Samir posts results. Short and concrete — prefer incremental rollout over big bang.
